▸2026-09-18GNRClong21dXLIAnchor customer contract reratingopen—
Generac (GNRC) 2026-09-16 (8-K, after the close): a Transaction Agreement with Amazon - a long-term supply agreement for backup power generators for Amazon data centers, with initial deliveries expected to total 2.4B USD across 2027 and 2028, plus a warrant issued to Amazon for up to 1,693,745 shares at an exercise price of 200.9266, of which 307,954 shares vested immediately and the rest vest in tranches against cumulative payments up to an 8B USD ceiling, exercisable to 2033. The read: GNRC is priced off residential standby demand and storm season, and the market had been DE-rating it into this news (close 190.21 on 9/8 to 175.11 on 9/16, roughly -8pct in a week on ordinary volume). The agreement replaces part of that weather-driven demand distribution with a dated delivery schedule from a named, capex-committed counterparty: 2.4B over two years against annual revenue near 4.3B is not a rounding item, and data-center C&I product carries better mix than home standby. The move on 9/17 was +18.3pct to 207.23 on 8.03M shares against roughly 1.2M normal (about 6.7x) - but it printed as much as +45pct after hours on 9/16 and gave back half of it, which is the signature of a market split between front-runners and wait-and-see rather than one that has repriced the multiple. The warrant strike at 200.93, set roughly 15pct above the undisturbed 175 price, is a dated public statement by an informed counterparty about where it expects the shares to go, and it is only barely below spot. RISK, and it is the whole bear case: 8B is a CEILING contingent on orders, not booked backlog - only the 2.4B tranche is scheduled - so a hyperscaler capex pause or a delivery slip strands the headline; the warrant is about 3pct dilution; and Amazon as an anchor customer owns the pricing power in every renewal. Event risk: no earnings inside a 21d window (GNRC reports Q3 late October, outside it); the live risks are order-flow headlines and the AI-capex tape. 21d fast sleeve: the catalyst is a discrete event pop whose drift, if it exists, resolves in weeks.

J.B. Hunt (JBHT) 2026-09-16: OFF-CYCLE cost warning at a Morgan Stanley conference (no earnings report, no change to demand guidance) - CFO flagged ~$25M incremental driver recruiting/training/bonus expense plus $10M+ of record-diesel headwind, implying Q3 EPS ~$1.77 vs ~$2.10 consensus. EVENT RISK: Q3 earnings land ~mid-October, INSIDE this 21d window, and can carry whatever else is wrong; diesel may keep climbing so the surcharge lag never closes; the gap day closed on its low with no absorption; freight recession has punished every prior turn call. Enova (ENVA) 2026-09-15: withdrew its OCC/Federal Reserve applications to acquire Grasshopper Bancorp, citing the absence of published regulatory standards for a nonbank seeking bank status. The lost bank charter was an OPTION on a lower future cost of funds (deposits vs warehouse/securitisation funding), never in guidance as earnings - so a markdown many times the deal's own cost is being applied to an operating business whose numbers did not change, while the freed cash becomes a price-insensitive buyer at the lower price. RISKS: (1) the withdrawal may be INFORMATION - if regulators are durably hostile to the nonbank-to-bank path, a permanently higher terminal cost of funds justifies a lower multiple on unchanged earnings and this is not an overreaction; (2) the stock had run hard into the event, so part of the drop is froth leaving rather than discount opening; (3) subprime consumer lender - reaffirmed earnings hold only until the credit cycle says otherwise, and a credit scare reprices the whole group; (4) no earnings inside the 21d window (Q3 print is late Oct, past expiry), so the window tests the repricing/buyback mechanism only, with no confirming catalyst. Casey's General Stores fiscal Q1 FY27 (rpt 9/8 post-close): beat BOTH lines - non-GAAP diluted EPS $7.37 vs $6.88 cons (+7%, and +27.7% YoY), total sales $5.68B +24.3% YoY (a hair under the $5.69B estimate), EBITDA +17.1%, the FIFTH consecutive EPS beat, driven by prepared-food sales, expanded inside margins AND a fuel-margin surge. A positive surprise was priced as if it were a cut, because a stock carrying a premium multiple treats the ABSENCE of a raise as news. RISKS, and they are real: the beat leaned on fuel margins, which are volatile and non-recurring, so the hold may be honest rather than conservative - analysts CUT price targets after the print; the multiple is still ~30x after the derate, so there is room for further compression that the guide being conservative would not stop; the tape has not stabilised (three consecutive lower closes, Friday closing near the day's low, the 9/9 gap-day low not yet tested) so entry timing is poor. Performance so far

This is the complete record of these predictions, not a highlight reel: each one is logged before its outcome and scored mechanically against a benchmark, wins and losses alike, and none are revised after the fact. One disclosed exception: an entry logged in July 2026 was withdrawn on 2026-09-13 because it was a personal note by the author, never a prediction of this project; it had not been scored. The project is at the hypothesis stage; no signal here has been shown to make money.

About

What this is

Swing Lab publishes stock market predictions before their outcomes are known. Each one names a company, a direction, a time window and the benchmark it has to beat, with the reasoning written down at the time. When the window closes, the result is scored automatically against that benchmark. Wins and losses both stay on the page, and nothing is revised afterwards. One entry was withdrawn in September 2026 because it was a personal note by the author rather than a prediction of this project; the Performance tab says so.

Where the figures come from

Prices are daily closing prices from public market data. A prediction's score is its own return over the window minus the benchmark's return over the same days, so a call only counts as a win when it did better than simply holding the benchmark. The scoring is done by code on a fixed daily schedule, not by hand, and the running total on the Performance tab is the sum of those scores.

Who makes it

Built by Guillermo Arria-Devoe as a research project in making predictions honestly: state the call first, let the outcome decide. The project is at the hypothesis stage and no method here has been shown to make money. Nothing on this page is investment advice.
